cells.tense: You hold what you chose to carry, even while it costs you something, right here.
cells.act: keep following the star after everything that has happened
cells.ask: Pick what you're still heading toward and stay with it one more day than usual. That extra day, and nothing promised beyond it.
cells.core:
You can hold on through strain — the long, unnecessary stretch of it — and still know with some precision what you're holding on toward. When something costs more than it should, you don't throw it away on the spot. You wait and see whether it still holds. That patience is yours; it isn't borrowed from anyone.

The want still points somewhere, even after what it has cost you. This week, pick whatever you're still heading toward and give it one more day than you normally would — nothing pledged beyond that day. You don't need a sign that it's working. Staying with it is the point.
cells.sheetLine: You can carry what you chose, even when it costs.
cells.place: a place held open toward what's genuinely wanted

cells.tense: You will carry the weight so long that carrying will look like the shape of you.
cells.act: let the exchange with someone run both ways
cells.ask: When a hand, a meal, or a yes comes your way this week, take it once and leave the count alone. Nothing given back to square it.
cells.core:
You're bracing for a weight that hasn't arrived yet. Where you carry toward what you want, everything gets measured by how much you can hold, and the number keeps climbing. You'll plan the next stretch before this one is done. The grip that looks like strength has become the whole posture.

The strength when it is real contains without crushing, and that includes you. So when a hand, a meal, a plain yes comes your way this week, take it once and leave the count alone — nothing given back to even it. One thing in, one left at that. Whatever you were bracing against can wait while you find out the hand holds.
cells.sheetLine: You'll carry more, because you can — until carrying is all you are.

cells.tense: You stood at a door that's already behind you, waiting to be seen there.
cells.act: do the giving in the open this time, where it was always done unseen
cells.ask: Find work you've done for someone while nobody watched. Do the next stretch of it where they can see you, and say nothing about it.
cells.core:
You have been holding things that nobody watched you hold — the unpaid hours, the early mornings, the small costs paid in private and unremarkable to anyone but you. The strength was there, and the visibility didn't catch up with it. That's the doorway you're at: everything sturdy, nothing to show for it.

There's a way back through this, and it isn't by doing more. Find work you've done for someone while nobody was watching, and do the next stretch of it in front of them — no explaining, no asking for credit. Let what you do land where it was aimed. Being watched isn't the reward. It's what lets the effort close.
cells.sheetLine: You gave and gave, and nobody saw you give.

cells.tense: The pen is down on a page you're still writing, and the hand on it has stopped looking like yours.
cells.act: carry on with the version you chose through another week of doubt
cells.ask: Put the aim you picked and why into one line you keep. Then carry it further without redeciding.
cells.core:
You can hold on through the hard stretch — that's yours, and you've done it more times than you'd list. What's harder to claim is that the aim was authored: the choice about what to head for gets carried quietly, filed under circumstances, under someone else's expectations, under how things turned out. Persisting gets the credit. Picking doesn't.

So write the aim you picked and why in one line, in your own hand, and keep that line — no rewriting it, no justifying it. Then carry the aim further as what it is: your pick, held. Not proof of anything. Just your choice, kept in your own hand one more turn of the road.
cells.sheetLine: Yours is what you keep, not what set it.
